title: t2579: make aidevops update auto-restart pulse + consolidate restart logic
body:
## Task

Make `aidevops update` (and `setup.sh --non-interactive`) automatically restart the pulse after deploying new scripts, so users pick up pulse-sourced code changes without manual `pkill + nohup` steps. Consolidate the duplicated restart logic currently living only in `_hotfix_auto_apply` into a shared `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`.

## Why

AGENTS.md (user-facing doc) already states:

> `setup.sh` and `aidevops update` handle this automatically via `_restart_pulse_if_running`. Interactive sessions deploying hotfixes via `cp` must restart manually.

But **the `_restart_pulse_if_running` function does not exist anywhere in the repo** — verified via `rg -n "_restart_pulse_if_running"` returning nothing. The claim is aspirational; the implementation is missing. Consequences:

- **Stale in-memory pulse code**: bash processes load `source` files at startup only. Updated `.sh` files deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` don't take effect until the pulse is restarted. Pulse fixes (lock races, rate-limit handling, dispatch logic) sit inert on disk while the running pulse keeps using the old code.
- **Multi-PID accumulation**: observed 2026-04-21 with 5 concurrent pulse PIDs because restarts never settle cleanly. The t2578 stale-lock fix exists and was merged, but users still have the old code running in memory.
- **Cross-runner drift**: remote runners pulling via `aidevops update` don't pick up pulse fixes either — same gap, wider surface.

Only the HOTFIX path (`_hotfix_auto_apply` in `aidevops-update-check.sh:408-443`) has restart logic, and it's inline/duplicated. Regular updates go through `cmd_update` → `setup.sh --non-interactive` → no restart.

## What

1. Create `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` as the canonical pulse lifecycle manager with subcommands:
   - `is-running` — exit 0 if any pulse PID, 1 otherwise
   - `stop` — SIGTERM all pulse instances, SIGKILL after grace window
   - `start` — nohup background start, check not already running
   - `restart` — stop + start (force, used for deploy scenarios)
   - `restart-if-running` — no-op if pulse not running, otherwise stop+start (used by update flow)
   - `status` — show PIDs + uptime (informational)

2. Call `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running` from:
   - `setup.sh` main() after `_setup_post_setup_steps` (catches all direct-setup paths, interactive and non-interactive)
   - `cmd_update` in `aidevops.sh` after setup succeeds (belt-and-braces)

3. Refactor `_hotfix_auto_apply` to call the shared helper instead of duplicating restart logic inline.

4. Honour `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1` env var as the opt-out (for active debugging sessions).

5. Add regression tests: `tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — verify each subcommand, the is-running check, env opt-out, and that restart survives a transient stop/start cycle.

## How

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — model on existing `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*-helper.sh` pattern (shebang, `set -euo pipefail`, subcommand dispatch, `main "$@"`).
- EDIT: `setup.sh` main() (after `_setup_post_setup_steps "$_os"`) — add single helper call.
- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` `cmd_update()` — add helper call after setup runs (both up-to-date-with-version-mismatch path and remote-ahead path).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` `_hotfix_auto_apply()` — replace inline restart block with helper call.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — update the "Pulse restart after deploying pulse script fixes" section to reflect that the behaviour is now actually implemented (keep the manual fallback documentation for developer hot-deploys).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — structural tests (subcommand dispatch, is-running detection, opt-out honoured, idempotent restart).
- Verification:
  - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` → all pass
  - `bash setup.sh --non-interactive` with pulse running → pulse restarts (new PID, old PID gone)
  - `bash setup.sh --non-interactive` with pulse stopped → no-op, no pulse started (respects "not running" state)
  - `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1 bash setup.sh --non-interactive` with pulse running → pulse NOT restarted
  - `shellcheck` clean on all modified files

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` exists with the 6 subcommands and is executable
- [ ] `setup.sh --non-interactive` restarts pulse when one is running
- [ ] `aidevops update` restarts pulse when updating (verified end-to-end with a live merged pulse-script change)
- [ ] `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1` opts out cleanly
- [ ] `_hotfix_auto_apply` no longer duplicates restart logic
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Pulse restart after deploying pulse script fixes" section matches reality
- [ ] Regression test passes: `test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all modified files
- [ ] No new function exceeds the 100-line complexity gate

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `setup.sh`
- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

## Session Origin

Interactive session (2026-04-21, maintainer) — user asked "how about we make it so aidevops update does that?" after observing t2578 (pulse stale-lock race) fix merged but 5 concurrent pulse PIDs still running because no restart happened. This is the canonical implementation of a long-documented-but-absent behaviour.

## Context

Tier: `tier:standard` — touches multiple core update-path files, needs reasoning about restart timing, env opt-out, and backward-compat with `_hotfix_auto_apply`. Not `tier:simple` because the design decisions (where to hook, naming, helper structure) need judgment, not just mechanical replacement.

title: Audit remaining local -n nameref usages for zsh-source compatibility gaps
body:
## Context

PR #20302 fixed one `local -n` nameref incompatibility in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (GH#20300). That fix exposed a broader question: which of the remaining 72 `local -n` usages across 6 deployed helpers are reachable from zsh-sourcing contexts, and therefore need the same pattern applied?

## Scope

This is a **research/audit task**, not a blanket rewrite. 72 sites is too many to fix indiscriminately — most will be reached only via shebang-invoked scripts where the re-exec guard in `shared-constants.sh:30-95` already kicks in (exec → Homebrew bash 4+ on macOS).

The question to answer: **which sites are sourced (not executed) from chains that could originate in zsh?**

That is the specific class of bug that caused GH#20300 — the re-exec guard relies on `BASH_VERSINFO` + `BASH_SOURCE[1]`, both unset when zsh sources a `.sh` file, so the guard never fires and the `local -n` declaration is then evaluated under zsh.

## Audit targets (accurate counts as of 2026-04-21, post-#20302-merge)

| File | Count | Initial reachability hypothesis |
|---|---:|---|
| `.agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh` | 43 | Heaviest user. Likely only executed (not sourced). Verify. |
| `.agents/scripts/email-delivery-test-helper.sh` | 12 | Likely only executed as a script; low risk. |
| `.agents/scripts/document-creation-helper.sh` | 11 | Check if sourced from any document workflows. |
| `.agents/scripts/setup/_tools.sh` | 2 | Sourced by `setup.sh` — verify `setup.sh` invocation origins. |
| `.agents/scripts/thumbnail-helper.sh` | 1 | Likely executed as a script. |
| `.agents/scripts/label-sync-helper.sh` | 1 | Likely executed as a script. |

## How

1. For each file, trace how it's invoked — shebang execution (safe, re-exec guard covers) vs. sourced from another script (potentially unsafe).
2. If a file is ever sourced, check whether that sourcing chain could originate from zsh (user's login shell sourcing `.sh` files via shell init, `aidevops` CLI wrapper chains, etc).
3. Apply the canonical module-globals pattern ONLY to sites that are demonstrably reachable from zsh-sourcing.
4. Document the reachability reasoning per file — "safe because X" is a valid outcome for most sites.

### Reference pattern

`.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh:638-770` — canonical module-globals pattern (`_BRIEF_*`). Key idea: the function sets module-level `_MODULE_VAR` globals; callers read them directly after invocation; no `local -n` declared inside the function body. Pattern-marker comments at `task-brief-helper.sh:643,757` and `linters-local.sh:1402` document this explicitly.

The specific transformation that PR #20302 applied to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:351-386`:

```bash
# Before (bash 4.3+ only — breaks under zsh):
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step() {
    local step="$1" input="$2"
    local -n _out_todo="$3" _out_title="$4"
    # ... sets _out_todo, _out_title via nameref
}

# After (bash 3.2 / zsh safe):
_GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TODO=""
_GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TITLE=""
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step() {
    local step="$1" input="$2"
    _GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TODO=""
    _GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TITLE=""
    # ... sets _GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_{TODO,TITLE} directly
}
```

### Verification per fix

Add a regression test modelled on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh` — exercise the function under zsh directly and assert the module globals are populated. Skip cleanly if `zsh` is not installed on the runner.

### macOS vs Linux coverage

- **macOS (bash 3.2 default, zsh as `/bin/sh`/login shell):** the highest-risk platform — the exact one GH#20300 surfaced on.
- **Legacy Linux (bash 3.2 containers):** same risk class without zsh, any `local -n` is a hard failure.
- **Modern Linux (bash 4+):** `local -n` works, no functional impact, but fixes are still valuable for uniformity.
- **Linux with zsh users:** same zsh-sourcing risk as macOS if they invoke framework helpers via sourced chains.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Per-file reachability analysis documented in follow-up comments or a dedicated decomposition doc
- [ ] Only genuinely-reachable sites get fixed (with documented justification per site)
- [ ] Unreachable sites documented as "safe — shebang-invoked only" with proof of how they're called
- [ ] Regression test per fixed file modelled on `test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh`
- [ ] The `bash 3.2 compatibility` regression gate counter drops by the number of sites fixed (from 82 post-#20302 down by N)

## Anti-scope

- **NOT** "rewrite all 72 sites." That's scope creep without evidence of reachability.
- **NOT** removing the canonical pattern-marker comments at `task-brief-helper.sh:643,757` or `linters-local.sh:1402` — those are the documentation of the pattern.
- **NOT** editing `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — already handled by PR #20302.

## Related

- Fix PR: #20302
- Original bug: #20300
- Re-exec guard (implementation): `shared-constants.sh:30-95`
- Canonical pattern: `task-brief-helper.sh:638-770`
- Regression test template: `test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh` (added in #20302)


## Children

- #20392 — Audit local -n nameref reachability for all 6 files (t2718, research phase)
- #20393 — Fix setup/_tools.sh local -n nameref usages, 2 sites at lines 96 and 126 (t2719, implementation phase)

_Decomposed by #20388. Hierarchy: audit first (documents which files are safe vs at-risk), then targeted fixes for at-risk files only._

title: t2685: harden gh signature-footer enforcement (PATH shim + plugin hook block)
body:
## What

The `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` output — with its `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` marker, runtime/version/model/token/session metadata, and canonical formatting — is the ONLY acceptable signature footer on GitHub writes. The framework has multiple enforcement paths, all defeatable:

1. **`gh_create_issue` / `gh_issue_comment` / `gh_create_pr` wrappers in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`** auto-inject the sig. Good when agents call these. Defeated by raw `gh` calls.
2. **OpenCode plugin hook `quality-hooks.mjs::checkSignatureFooterGate`** inspects tool calls before execution. Defeated by its current trust check: `cmd.includes("aidevops.sh")` — any string containing the literal domain passes, including hallucinated prose that mentions the domain.
3. **`build.txt` §8 prompt rule** instructs agents to call the helper and never compose inline. Prompt-layer rule only — no hard enforcement.

On 2026-04-21 an interactive cleanup session on a managed private repo (webapp) posted a human-readable footer (`"— interactive cleanup from marcusquinn runtime."`) with no `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` marker and no runtime metadata. All three layers silently allowed it through.

## Why

Hallucinated footers defeat the observability contract — without runtime/version/model fields, we can't trace issues to the session that produced them, correlate outcomes to model tiers, or identify regressions by runtime version. This is a correctness defect in the signature-footer enforcement system, not a cosmetic nit.

## How

Three structural fixes, in order of trust:

1. **PATH shim at `.agents/scripts/gh`** — intercepts `gh issue comment|create` and `gh pr comment|create`, auto-injects `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` output when body lacks the canonical marker. Bypass: `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`. Fast pass-through for all other subcommands.

2. **Tighten `checkSignatureFooterGate`** — replace loose `cmd.includes("aidevops.sh")` with marker-based detection (`<!-- aidevops:sig -->`). Transparent repair via `output.args.command` mutation. Throw mentoring Error on unparseable bodies (heredoc-sourced etc.).

3. **Reinforce `build.txt` §8** — anti-pattern section quoting the exact hallucinated prose structure.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/gh` (PATH shim, shellcheck clean)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs` (tighten gate logic)
- EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` §8 (add anti-pattern example)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/_deployment.sh` (chmod +x shim after deploy)

## Acceptance

- [x] All three layers (shim, plugin hook, prompt rule) refuse a hallucinated footer body.
- [x] `gh-signature-helper.sh footer`-generated bodies pass all three layers unmodified.
- [x] Bypass env var (`AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`) works for local diagnosis.
- [x] Regression test coverage: existing `test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` still passes (30/30).

## Session Origin

- **Branch:** feature/t2685-gh-signature-enforcement
- **Runtime:** OpenCode v1.14.19
- **Conversation:** interactive, triggered by a hallucinated footer incident on a managed private repo during a duplicate-nudge cleanup session on 2026-04-21.

title: bug: 'Prompt guard patterns: Nd old' warning never clears — rsync -a preserves source mtime, so 'aidevops update' is a no-op for the check
body:
## Description

The security startup check `check_prompt_guard_patterns` in
`security-posture-helper.sh` flags the deployed patterns YAML as stale whenever
its **file mtime** is >30 days old, and recommends `aidevops update` as the fix.

However, `deploy_aidevops_agents` (`setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh`) uses
`rsync -a`, which preserves source mtime on copy. If upstream hasn't modified
`.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` in >30 days, re-deploying
copies the same mtime back — and the warning fires again on the next session.

This creates a circular loop visible to any user whose system is fully up to
date during an upstream quiet period:

1. Session start warns: `Prompt guard patterns: 36d old (>30d)`
2. `aidevops security setup` offers: `Run: aidevops update`
3. Update reports: `Framework already up to date!` (correct — content matches)
4. mtime unchanged → warning fires again on next session

The user has no action they can take. The patterns file IS the current
upstream version; the staleness signal is measuring upstream release cadence,
not local drift.

## Expected Behavior

One of the following (maintainers to decide):

- **Option A — touch on confirmed-current deploy.** After `deploy_aidevops_agents`
  completes and the deployed SHA matches upstream HEAD, `touch` the patterns
  YAML so mtime reflects "last confirmed current" rather than "last upstream edit".
- **Option B — compare against upstream commit date, not mtime.** Use
  `git log -1 --format=%ct -- configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` from the
  canonical repo (or the `.deployed-sha` stamp at `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha`)
  as the reference point. If upstream itself hasn't shipped a patterns update
  in 30d, the check is informational at best.
- **Option C — reframe the warning.** "No upstream updates in 30d" is not an
  actionable staleness signal when the local copy already matches upstream.
  Suppress the warning when local == upstream, or promote it to an advisory
  (`[--]` rather than `[!!]`) rather than an action-needed item.

Option A is the smallest delta and preserves the "30 days since we refreshed
your patterns" semantic. Option B is the most correct (measures what it claims
to measure). Option C is the cheapest if the maintainers consider the check
low-value once the other signals (secret storage, gh auth, secretlint) are in.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
aidevops security setup
```

**Actual output**:

```
Security Setup
===============

Walking through pending security actions.

[1] Prompt guard patterns: 36d old (>30d)
    Run: aidevops update

    Run aidevops update now? [Y/n]

Updating AI DevOps Framework

[INFO] Current version: 3.8.88
[INFO] Fetching latest version...
[OK] Framework already up to date!
...
=======================================
Fixed: 1 action(s)
=======================================
```

Next `aidevops security setup` invocation reports the same `36d old` warning.
`Fixed: 1 action(s)` is itself misleading — nothing was fixed; the underlying
file mtime was not updated.

**Expected output**: either no staleness warning (file matches upstream HEAD),
or a warning that clears after a successful update.

**Causal code**:

`~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh` lines 947-983
(`check_prompt_guard_patterns`):

```bash
# Check staleness (>30 days old)
local file_age_days=0
if [[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    file_mod=$(stat -f %m "$yaml_file" || echo "0")
    now=$(date +%s)
    file_age_days=$(((now - file_mod) / 86400))
else
    file_age_days=$((($(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$yaml_file" || echo "0")) / 86400))
fi

if [[ "$file_age_days" -gt 30 ]]; then
    CHECK_LABEL="$label: ${file_age_days}d old (>30d)"
    CHECK_FIX="Run: aidevops update"
    return 1
fi
```

`~/Git/aidevops/setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` line 141 and the
`_atomic_stage_and_deploy_agents` helper both use `rsync -a`, which preserves
source mtime.

No recent commits (last 2 weeks) touch either
`.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh` or
`.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `aidevops update` when upstream hasn't touched
   `.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` for >30 days (current
   upstream file was last touched 2026-03-15 by commit `c091cc6e1`).
2. Start a new session — security greeting says N actions needed.
3. Run `aidevops security setup` — offered fix is `Run: aidevops update`.
4. Accept; update reports "Framework already up to date!".
5. Re-run `aidevops security setup` — same warning, same offered fix.

## Workarounds Applied

None landed — there is no user-side workaround. A user could manually
`touch ~/.aidevops/agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` to suppress
the warning for another 30 days, but this is a local patch for a framework
bug and must not be recommended because it defeats the check's intent: any
real staleness after a subsequent upstream release would still be masked
until that file hits 30d again.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.88
- **Latest version**: 3.8.88
- **Install method**: `~/.local/bin/aidevops` → `~/Git/aidevops/aidevops.sh` (git symlink)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode v1.14.19 with claude-opus-4-7
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (VirtualBox guest)
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

## Additional Context

- Deployed file: `~/.aidevops/agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`
  mtime 2026-03-16 10:58, 27535 bytes.
- Source file: `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`
  mtime 2026-03-16 10:58, 27535 bytes. Content matches.
- Last upstream commit touching this file: `c091cc6e1` on 2026-03-15.
- `Change` time on the deployed file is 2026-04-21 11:16 (today's update),
  confirming rsync ran but preserved the source `Modify` time.
- Stamp file `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha` already exists for t2156 drift
  detection, so Option B can reuse it without new infrastructure.

title: bug: /log-issue-aidevops allows duplicate filings — search indexing lag + no idempotency in gh issue create
body:
## Description

The `/log-issue-aidevops` command and its backing `log-issue-helper.sh search` subcommand have a **race window** between the duplicate-check step and the issue-creation step that permits duplicate issue filings from a single user session. There is **no body-hash fingerprint**, **no idempotency on `gh issue create`**, and **no recent-by-author filtering** — dedup is entirely dependent on GitHub's search index having caught up, which it often hasn't.

The duplicate-check itself (Step 3 in the command doc) uses `gh issue list --search "KEYWORDS"`, which:

1. Hits GitHub's search index, which has a **2-10 second indexing lag** after an issue is created.
2. Is **agent-driven** — the LLM composes the keywords. Identical-body submissions with differently-chosen keywords will miss each other.
3. Is **not atomic with creation** — even if Step 3 returns zero hits, Step 6 runs `gh issue create` with no further check.

On a `gh issue create` transient failure (network timeout, 5xx), the agent or the user retrying will create a second issue — the first may have succeeded server-side. There is no reconciliation.

## Expected Behavior

One of the following (maintainers to decide — all three can coexist):

- **Option A — body-hash fingerprint file.** Before `gh issue create`, hash `(title + body + author)` and look it up in `~/.aidevops/state/log-issue-fingerprints.jsonl` (timestamp + issue number). If the same fingerprint was filed in the last N seconds (suggest 60), either (a) abort with "you filed this N seconds ago: #NNN" or (b) `gh issue comment` on the prior issue instead of creating a new one. Append on success. This is **deterministic** and not subject to search indexing lag.

- **Option B — `gh_create_issue` wrapper with built-in idempotency.** Wrap `gh issue create` in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` so that every call first runs `gh issue list --author @me --search "<title-verbatim>" --created ">$(date -d '-60s' --iso-8601=seconds)"` and short-circuits if a match exists. Opt-out flag for intentional sequential filings (`--allow-duplicate`).

- **Option C — recent-by-author pre-check in `/log-issue-aidevops`.** Step 3 currently does a keyword search across all issues/all states. Add a second check: `gh issue list --author @me --state open --created '>PT5M'` — anything this user filed in the last 5 minutes that has a >80% title match is a likely dup. Deterministic, no state file needed.

Option A is the most robust (works across sessions, surviving process crashes). Option B automates it at the API surface (wider blast radius — affects every `gh_create_issue` caller, not just `/log-issue-aidevops`). Option C is the cheapest and most targeted.

## Reproducer

**Live reproducer** (both open in repo, one now closed as dup):

- #20312 — created 2026-04-21T16:07:58Z by @robstiles
- #20313 — created 2026-04-21T16:08:10Z by @robstiles (closed as dup)

**Byte-identical bodies**. **12-second gap** between filings. Same session (identical signature-footer metadata: "13m and 29,474 tokens"). GitHub's search index did not surface #20312 when #20313 was about to be filed — OR the dedup check wasn't run — OR the first `gh issue create` returned an error that masked its server-side success.

**Ironically**, the `github-actions[bot]` auto-response on both issues says:

> Tip: For faster, higher-quality issue reporting, use `/log-issue-aidevops` in your AI assistant session. It gathers diagnostics automatically and checks for duplicates.

The "checks for duplicates" claim is the failure mode — dedup ran (or was supposed to run) and still produced two copies.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From an AI assistant session, invoke `/log-issue-aidevops` with any framework bug report.
2. After Step 4 composes the body, let the agent retry the `gh issue create` call twice in rapid succession (or simulate by running the same `gh issue create` command twice manually within 10 seconds).
3. Two issues are filed with identical bodies. The second Step 3 run, if done within indexing lag, does not find the first.

**Alternative reproducer** (explicit race): two concurrent sessions run `/log-issue-aidevops` on the same bug within 5 seconds. Both pass Step 3 (empty results) and both file. Not yet observed but structurally possible.

## Causal Code

**Command doc** — `.agents/scripts/commands/log-issue-aidevops.md`:

- Lines 115-121 (Step 3): agent-driven `gh issue list --search` with no post-creation verification.
- Lines 243-253 (Step 6): `gh issue create` with no idempotency wrapper.

**Helper** — `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh`:

- Lines 167-183 (`search_issues()`): thin wrapper over `gh issue list --search`, no fingerprint lookup.
- No `filed_recently()`, no `fingerprint_lookup()`, no `check_not_recently_filed()` subcommand exists.

**Wrapper** — `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (for Option B): `gh_create_issue` currently has no idempotency logic — if it did, Option B would be near-free.

## Workarounds Applied

During this session I hit two adjacent framework gaps while investigating:

1. **`isGhWriteCommand` false-positive** (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:47-55`): the regex `\bgh\s+(pr\s+(create|comment)|issue\s+(create|comment))\b` matches the literal text `gh issue create` inside a `--search` argument value, blocking legitimate read commands like `gh issue list --search "idempotency gh issue create"`. Workaround: reword the search string. Root cause: regex doesn't distinguish command body from quoted argument content. File as sibling issue if confirmed.

2. **Plugin module caching**: on first session attempt, the patched `quality-hooks.mjs` was on disk but OpenCode's cached module still had the broken version — bash was 100% blocked. Required a fresh process (not just a new session). Already addressed by t2693/#20320.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.91 (post-t2693 patch)
- **Observed duplicates**: #20312 and #20313 (see Reproducer)
- **OS**: macOS (investigation) — bug is OS-agnostic, platform doesn't matter for the race
- **Reporter of duplicates**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (per #20312 environment)

## Additional Context

- The `/log-issue-aidevops` command doc's Step 3 admonishes the agent to "present them and ask" when duplicates are found. This is a **soft gate** — the agent can skip it or miss matches. Any durable fix must be deterministic (file-system or API-level), not agent-driven.
- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` exists for worker dispatch and implements layered deterministic checks. An analogous `issue-create-dedup-helper.sh` with fingerprint + recent-window + author-filter would be the natural pattern match.
- Sibling issue territory (optional split-out):
  - `isGhWriteCommand` regex false-positive on quoted arguments
  - `gh issue create` idempotency in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (Option B above, as its own task)

title: aidevops update: redeploy on .deployed-sha drift, not just VERSION/sentinel
body:
## Task

Make `aidevops update` self-heal deployed-script drift on EVERY merge to main — not just on version bumps or changes to one sentinel file.

## Why

Observed 2026-04-21: `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha` lagged `origin/main` by 6 commits for ~14h, including PR #20323 (t2695) which fixed `gh search prs --headRefName` — a bug crashing the pulse batch prefetch every ~4 minutes. The auto-updater runs every 10 min but two blind spots prevented redeployment:

1. **`aidevops.sh::cmd_update`** (line 550-560) — when `local_hash == remote_hash` (git already up to date), only compares `VERSION` files. `VERSION` bumps on releases only, so post-release merges never trigger `setup.sh --non-interactive`.

2. **`auto-update-helper.sh::_cmd_check_stale_agent_redeploy`** (line 1326-1340) — compares SHA-256 of a single sentinel file (`gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`). If the merged fix touches a different file (like `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`), drift is invisible.

`.deployed-sha` IS written correctly by `setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh:612`. `_check_script_drift` in `aidevops-update-check.sh` already does the right check — but it only fires on interactive session start via `_run_session_advisories`, not from headless auto-update paths.

## How

Replace both blind-spot checks with a `.deployed-sha`-based comparison that catches any framework code change:

- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` — in `cmd_update`, after the `local_hash == remote_hash` branch's VERSION check, also compare `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha` against `$local_hash`. If drifted AND the drift includes framework code paths (`.agents/scripts/`, `agents/`, `workflows/`, `prompts/`, `hooks/`), run `setup.sh --non-interactive`. Docs-only drift is skipped.

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh` — in `_cmd_check_stale_agent_redeploy`, replace the single-sentinel SHA-256 check with the same `.deployed-sha` stamp check. Keep the VERSION check as the first gate (cheaper).

### Files Scope

- aidevops.sh
- .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-cmd-update-sha-drift.sh

## Acceptance

- Staling `.deployed-sha` to a prior SHA and running `aidevops update` triggers `setup.sh --non-interactive`, verified by stamp advancing to current `HEAD`.
- The check only fires when framework code files drift (not docs-only).
- Existing VERSION-mismatch path continues to work.
- Regression test covering: no-drift, code-drift triggers redeploy, docs-only drift skipped, missing stamp skipped.

## Context

- Root cause investigation: memory mem_20260421190735_390b100f (2026-04-21 high)
- Prior attempt: t2156 (PR #19462) — added the detector + stamp writer; this PR completes the loop by wiring the detector into `aidevops update` / auto-update-helper instead of only interactive session start.

title: Review followup: PR #20354 — GH#20327: t2698: seed TODO.md entries for open orphan GitHub issues in pull
body:
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions

PR #20354 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment
below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline
review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was
flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's
GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether
the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue
with a wontfix rationale.

**Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20354

---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `prompts/build.txt`
section 6a). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.

Prefer using python3 for robust URL encoding to handle unicode correctly and avoid potential jq version compatibility problems.

> _query="${_query}&labels=$(python3 -c 'import sys, urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.stdin.read().strip()))' <<< "$_labels_csv")"
> ```

title: t2717: fix: replace misleading 'high/critical' aggregate label in quality-sweep dashboard with per-severity breakdown
body:
Dashboard label '(N high/critical)' is mislabelling the MAJOR+CRITICAL+BLOCKER aggregate count. MAJOR is a CODE_SMELL severity in SonarCloud's taxonomy, not a high-severity signal. When live counts are (0 BLOCKER, 0 CRITICAL, 98 MAJOR), the current label shows '(98 high/critical)' which is misleading — there are zero truly-high-severity findings. Fix: plumb a per-severity inline string through _sweep_sonarcloud_issues → _sweep_sonarcloud_wrapper → _update_quality_issue_body → _build_quality_issue_body, and render '(N BLOCKER · N CRITICAL · N MAJOR · N MINOR)' in the dashboard row instead of the misleading aggregate. Keep high_critical_count in state file untouched for backward-compat with existing tests and state files.

title: t2724: route session-start framework status to TUI toast instead of message context
body:
## What

Render the session-start framework status as an OpenCode TUI toast via `client.tui.showToast()` instead of (or in addition to) injecting it as the first message in context. Phase 1 is additive — the toast appears alongside the existing message-context greeting so we can A/B the visual result. Phase 2 trims the human-only parts from the context version.

## Why

The current session greeting — version string, security advisories, pulse status, contribution count — is rendered by the model as the first message in every interactive session. This consumes 100-200 tokens of context per session (more when advisories are active), even though most of the content is status information the human needs but the model rarely acts on.

OpenCode 1.14 exposes `client.tui.showToast()` (SDK method `TuiShowToastData`, URL `/tui/show-toast`) with `variant: info|success|warning|error` and optional `duration`. Routing the banner through toasts frees that context entirely while keeping the human-visible information at session start.

## How

Phase 1 — additive plugin hook:

- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs` — module exporting `createGreetingHook({ scriptsDir, client })`. Handler fires on `event.type === "session.created"`, guarded by a `fired` flag so it runs once per plugin init. Runs `${scriptsDir}/aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive`, parses the output into up to 3 toasts (info for version/env, warning for pulse/contribution, error for security advisories), emits via `await client.tui.showToast({ body: { title, message, variant, duration } })`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — import `createGreetingHook`, compose the greeting handler into the existing `event:` hook alongside the observability handler so both run on every event.
- Model pattern to follow: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs` (same event-subscription style; see `handleEvent` signature).
- Defaults: 3 toasts max, 10s duration (30s for errors), fire-once per plugin init.

Phase 2 — trim redundant human-only lines from model-rendered greeting (separate commit in same PR once Phase 1 is visually confirmed):

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh:47-…` — the "On interactive conversation start" instruction block. Reduce to: "If the user asks about version/advisories/status, Read `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt`." Remove the "greet with: Hi!..." scripted response entirely (toast handles it).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh`
- `todo/tasks/*-brief.md`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance

- Launching a fresh OpenCode session displays an info toast within 2s of first prompt render showing the aidevops version and runtime.
- When security advisories are present, a separate error-variant toast appears with the advisory summary.
- When the pulse is stalled or contributions need reply, a warning-variant toast appears.
- Message-context consumption from the greeting drops by ≥50 tokens (measured via `opencode stats` before/after a clean session start with no advisories).
- No regression: the existing observability `event:` handler still receives all events (verified via `~/.aidevops/logs/observability.sqlite` new rows on tool calls).
- Plugin init completes without errors in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` or OpenCode's own log.

## Session Origin

Interactive session, OpenCode v1.14.20, aidevops v3.8.91. Request from maintainer — "shall we add to toast first, see how that looks, then remove bit by bit that's for humans only?"
